summary: Intermittent traffic routed to us-east for EU-locked tenant after control-plane sync
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (AtlasPay) reports intermittent requests appearing in us-east even though their tenant is pinned to eu-west. This began after a scheduled control-plane configuration sync on 2026-03-04.

Impact:
- Customer is seeing 20-40% of requests routed to us-east for short windows (30s-2m).
- Observed higher p95/p99 e2e latency for impacted requests and occasional auth handshake retries.
- No error responses returned to clients, but increased latency and unexpected network egress to a different region (cost + data residency concerns).

Timeline / Observations:
- 2026-03-04 02:00 UTC: control-plane config sync rolled to region routing service for eu-west tenants (canary -> full).
- 2026-03-04 02:01-02:03 UTC: AtlasPay reported a spike in p99 and notified Support.
- 2026-03-04 02:05 UTC: Support opened this ticket. Logs show a subset of requests selected us-east edges.
- 2026-03-04 02:10-02:12 UTC: Control-plane metrics show brief re-evaluation of routing policy for ~2k tenants.

Environment:
- Customer: dedicated account with pinned_region=eu-west.
- Frontend: api-gateway edge clusters in eu-west and us-east.
- Control plane: routing service v1.18.1 (deployed 2026-03-03).

Steps to reproduce (customer workflow):
1) Send a batch of 100 requests from client in EU to Redwood API using their API key.
2) Observe request-level edge selection in the response headers (X-Redwood-Edge) and latency telemetry.
3) Repeat during next control-plane sync window (approx every 6h).

Observed behavior:
- Randomized subset of requests receive X-Redwood-Edge: us-east-01, even though the token is stamped eu-west.
- These requests exhibit ~120-250ms higher network latency + additional auth handshake time (TLS + token verification).

Expected behavior:
- All requests for the pinned tenant should route to eu-west edges unless a deterministic failover to a configured alternate region is triggered by capacity constraints.

Troubleshooting performed so far:
- Validated tenant routing metadata: tenant.pin_region == eu-west.
- Cross-checked control-plane logs for delta during deploy window; found short-lived worker restart spikes.
- Compared token region stamp vs selected edge: in some cases the token stamp and selected edge mismatched.
- Confirmed no quota/usage-based fallback triggered on customer account.
- Confirmed no scheduled maintenance in eu-west at that time.

Relevant logs/snippets (redacted):
- control-plane/routing-engine: "Reconcile tenant=atlaspay: pin_region=eu-west assigned_edges=eu-west; transient evaluation took 24ms"
- edge-proxy/us-east-01: "Accepted request key=*** from tenant=atlaspay token_region=eu-west"
- auth-service: "TokenValidation: ok token_region=eu-west, issued_at=2026-03-04T01:59:55Z"

Hypothesis so far:
- A race during control-plane sync: routing policy reconciliation briefly returns an empty candidate set for eu-west edges for some shards, and edge-selection service falls back to global default (us-east) instead of honoring the token stamp.
- TTL/staleness in the edge affinity cache (local N-1 caches) might cause an inconsistent view across gateway instances.

Requested action from Engineering/SRE:
- Review control-plane reconcile path for tenant routing when assigned_edges is empty or nil; ensure fallback respects token_region header.
- Check for cache invalidation propagation windows between routing service and edge proxies during deploys.
- Audit edge-selection codepath for a deterministic prefer-token-region policy.

Customer notes (from AtlasPay):
- This is impacting a small percentage of payment-related calls; they have regulatory constraints about cross-border egress. They request an ETA on root cause and a mitigation (preferably a quick guard to never route off-region for their tenant).

2026-03-06 11:20 - Priya Rao (Routing Eng): Found a code path where candidate_edges list is treated as empty during a rare reconciliation confluence. Patch prepared to enforce prefer-token-region when candidate_edges empty. PR linked.

investigation_notes: Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-control-plane/pull/942 - enforces fallback to token_region when assigned_edges is empty.
Cache invalidation trace shows ~10-15s propagation on one shard due to backpressure from metrics exporter; this aligns with observed 30s-2m windows when combined with client side retries.
Auth stamps are correct in all observed cases; mismatch appears post-routing decision, not auth verification.
